beginner/identity/authentication-vs-auth.notes: A real session token must be long and random; the demo's numbered tokens are now explained. Slide typo '?.' fixed.
BCrypt cost 4 is the lowest setting, used only for speed; a real shop uses 10 or more.
Removed the 'pkce' tag: PKCE is not covered in this video.

beginner/passwords-and-mfa/password-atta.notes: Per account-and-address locks allow 50 guesses before all ten are locked, not before any is.
The burst passes at once only with nodelay; 429 comes from limit_req_status, nginx's default is 503.

beginner/passwords-and-mfa/totp-multi-fa.notes: No corrections needed; RFC 4226 and 6238 values checked.
No corrections needed; java-otp 1.0.0 validateOneTimePassword confirmed.

beginner/cryptography/symmetric-encrypti.notes: 2^32 is NIST's limit for random nonces under one key, not the point where a repeat becomes likely (that is near 2^48).
YouTube description now says envelope encryption, which is what the video shows.

beginner/cryptography/asymmetric-encrypt.notes: Modern (TLS 1.3) HTTPS, not every HTTPS connection, begins with key agreement. Slide typo '?.' fixed.
The JDK reads X.509 certificates and has a JDK 25 PEM preview; addProvider is global but does not change existing algorithms; jdk15on/jdk18on are artifact names, not package names.

beginner/cryptography/digital-signatures.notes: Only Android's original (v1) APK signing uses CMS, like jarsigner.

beginner/cryptography/keystore-basics.notes: A PKCS12 file stores the key's alias as UTF-16 text: the name is visible. Code, test, output and narration corrected.

beginner/networking/tcp-ip-basics.notes: SYN cookies carry a few options (the MSS always), not none.

beginner/networking/tcp-ip-basics-with-t.notes: Floods often forge random addresses, so they are found by unfinished handshakes, not by one network. Live capture needs special rights, usually root.

beginner/networking/dns-basics.notes: Encrypted DNS protects the path to the resolver, not the resolver's own lookups.

beginner/networking/dns-basics-with-core.notes: DNSSEC catches records forged on the way, but signs whatever is in the zone, wrong records too.

beginner/networking/http-basics-and-head.notes: SameSite limits cross-site sending; Lax still sends on top-level links.

beginner/transport-security/certificates.notes: The animation showed a name-constraint refusal and a revocation refusal in red; both are the defence working, now green. 'Another bank' reworded.

beginner/safe-habits/least-privilege.notes: The SecurityManager is permanently disabled since JDK 24 (JEP 486), not removed.

beginner/safe-habits/backups-and-recover.notes: YouTube title shortened to 99 characters (the limit is 100).
